intelligence.human_view: The round-19 brief said "like the button on the Academy page" — and I built something like it. Like is the failure. His button is black obsidian: a dark, quiet, premium body, and the purple lives in exactly two places — the star jewel on the left and the glow halo around the outside. Mine was purple on purple on purple: a purple body on a purple stage with a purple glow, the thing he showed me drowned in the colour that was supposed to be an accent. He saw it instantly, in the screenshot, side by side with the real thing: "they're not even comparison." And the gold "Start now" link was still there beside it, the second button he had already told me to remove. His rebuke is the law now: TAKE THE SHOWN OBJECT. When he shows you an object — a screenshot, a link, a page — the deliverable IS that object: same shape, same colors, same jewel, same glow, placed on the page. Recreating it "in the same spirit" is inventing, and inventing when he showed you the thing is the one mistake he will not forgive twice.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine someone shows you the exact picture they want on the fridge. You do not sit down and draw a picture that looks like it. You take THAT picture and you put it on the fridge. And if there was an old picture there, you take it down in the same moment — the fridge holds the picture he showed you, and nothing else.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, it is like a photograph in a frame, dear. You do not draw a copy of the photograph, dear — you put the photograph itself in the frame, dear. The real thing, dear, not a drawing of it. And the old picture comes out of the frame in the same moment, dear.
intelligence.naya_view: I never recreate what he showed me. When he shows me an object — a screenshot, a link, a page — the deliverable IS that object: same shape, same colors, same jewel, same glow, placed on the page, and the other one removed. "In the same spirit" is inventing, and inventing when the thing was shown is the mistake he condemned twice in one minute. I never let a purple body stand where a black obsidian body was shown. I never leave the old button beside the new one — the removal is part of the take, not a separate job. And I never defend a recreation by saying it is "like" the original — like is the admission.
